PCl5 and sp3d hybridization
Tip: switch to orbitals and click any orange lobe; rotate the scene to see the trigonal bipyramid.
Molecular geometry
The default view shows PCl5 as a ball-and-stick trigonal bipyramid: two axial chlorine atoms above and below phosphorus, and three equatorial chlorine atoms around the middle.

plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating sp3d hybridization in phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5) at the molecular and orbital levels. Panel (a) shows a ball-and-stick model of PCl5 with an orange phosphorus atom at the center covalently bonded to five green chlorine atoms directed toward the vertices of a trigonal bipyramid: two axial Cl atoms situated above and below the central P atom along a vertical axis, and three equatorial Cl atoms arranged symmetrically in the horizontal plane. Panel (b) depicts the five sp3d hybrid orbitals that account for these five bonds, each shown as a large orange lobe radiating from a central black dot representing the phosphorus nucleus, labeled "sp3d," and arranged in the same trigonal bipyramidal pattern with dashed lines connecting the lobe tips to outline the geometry; small back-lobes are omitted for clarity. This figure establishes sp3d hybridization — derived from mixing one 3s, three 3p, and one 3d orbital of phosphorus — as the valence-bond explanation for the five equivalent bonding regions in PCl5 and connects orbital theory directly to the observed trigonal bipyramidal molecular structure.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The same trigonal-bipyramidal arrangement appears as either five P-Cl bond directions or five sp3d hybrid orbitals.
Each sp3d lobe points along one specific bonding direction, so selecting a lobe identifies the corresponding axial or equatorial P-Cl bond.
Rotating the model reveals that the two axial positions are opposite each other and perpendicular to the three equatorial positions.

demo_steps.narration: The default view shows PCl5 as a ball-and-stick trigonal bipyramid: two axial chlorine atoms above and below phosphorus, and three equatorial chlorine atoms around the middle.

demo_steps.title: Orbital explanation
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the hybrid-orbital view. The five sp3d lobes occupy the same five directions as the five P-Cl bonds.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use one shared 3D coordinate frame so the molecular bonds and hybrid orbitals align exactly. Approximate scale: central P sphere radius 0.28 world units; Cl sphere radius 0.34; P-Cl bond length to Cl center about 1.55; bond cylinders radius 0.08. Put phosphorus at (0, 0, 0). Use +Y as the vertical axial direction in the source image: axial Cl atoms at (0, +1.55, 0) and (0, -1.55, 0). Put the three equatorial directions in the XZ plane: right equatorial Cl at (+1.55, 0, 0), upper-left/back equatorial Cl at (-0.775, 0, +1.342), and lower-left/front equatorial Cl at (-0.775, 0, -1.342). These three equatorial directions are 120° apart, and the axial directions are 90° from the equatorial plane. For the source-like orientation, frame the scene so +Y appears vertical, +X appears screen-right, and ±Z separate the two left equatorial bonds into upper-left and lower-left depths. Molecular colors: phosphorus orange #d8731c, chlorine green #36b44a with yellow-green highlights #8bd94a, bond orange #f08224 near P and green #3fad4c near Cl. Hybrid orbital lobes: five elongated teardrop/ovoid lobes along the same five unit vectors, length about 1.55 to 1.75 from center, maximum radius about 0.36 to 0.45, translucent orange-yellow #f6b24a with lighter yellow highlights #ffd37a and orange rim #e58a2a. The orbital diagram should omit small back-lobes. Dashed geometry lines are olive green #82a83b, thin, connecting the five lobe tips as a trigonal-bipyramidal outline: top axial tip to each equatorial tip, bottom axial tip to each equatorial tip, with visible screen-facing edges emphasized. Internal dashed centerlines run from near the nucleus toward each lobe tip. Labels are black italic 'sp³d' near each lobe: top label above/right of upper axial lobe, right label to the right of right lobe, bottom label below lower axial lobe, and two labels to the left of the upper-left and lower-left lobes. Selected lobe and matching bond should turn brighter yellow/gold #ffd400 and optionally gain a thin outline/glow.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement the toggle by showing one complete panel at a time rather than placing both panels side by side initially. Preserve the same camera and coordinate frame when switching views so the correspondence is visually obvious. For click selection in the hybrid-orbital view, raycast against the five lobe meshes; store the selected direction index and apply the same highlight index to the molecular bond when the learner toggles back to the molecular model. Labels can be CSS2D or sprite text with superscript formatting for sp³d. Use smooth shaded spheres/cylinders for panel (a), and custom elongated ellipsoid or metaball-like meshes for the lobes in panel (b).

authoredContext:
In a molecule of phosphorus pentachloride, PCl 5 , there are five P–Cl bonds (thus five pairs of valence electrons around the phosphorus atom) directed toward the corners of a trigonal bipyramid. We use the 3 s orbital, the three 3 p orbitals, and one of the 3 d orbitals to form the set of five sp 3 d hybrid orbitals ( ) that are involved in the P–Cl bonds. Other atoms that exhibit sp 3 d hybridization include the sulfur atom in SF 4 and the chlorine atoms in ClF 3 and in ClF 4 + . (The electrons on fluorine atoms are omitted for clarity.)

(a) The five regions of electron density around phosphorus in PCl 5 require five hybrid sp 3 d orbitals. (b) These orbitals combine to form a trigonal bipyramidal structure with each large lobe of the hybrid orbital pointing at a vertex. As before, there are also small lobes pointing in the opposite direction for each orbital (not shown for clarity).

Two images are shown and labeled “a” and “b.” Image a depicts a ball-and-stick model in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement. Image b depicts the hybrid orbitals in the same arrangement and each is labeled, “s p superscript three d.”

The sulfur atom in sulfur hexafluoride, SF 6 , exhibits sp 3 d 2 hybridization. A molecule of sulfur hexafluoride has six bonding pairs of electrons connecting six fluorine atoms to a single sulfur atom. There are no lone pairs of electrons on the central atom. To bond six fluorine atoms, the 3 s orbital, the three 3 p orbitals, and two of the 3 d orbitals form six equivalent sp 3 d 2 hybrid orbitals, each directed toward a different corner of an octahedron. Other atoms that exhibit sp 3 d 2 hybridization include the phosphorus atom in PCl 6 − , the iodine atom in the interhalogens IF 6 + , IF 5 , ICl 4 − , IF 4 − and the xenon atom in XeF 4 .

discrepancies: The default molecular view highlights the axial-up chlorine atom and bond in yellow, while the source molecule has all chlorine atoms green with no selected/highlighted bond.
The initial molecule orientation does not closely match the source: the equatorial atoms project as left/right/back rather than the source's one right and two left-side equatorial positions.
The two textbook panels are implemented as a toggle rather than shown side by side, so the default view lacks the immediate comparative composition of the original figure.
The generated molecule uses glossy highlight spheres and stronger 3D lighting effects that are not present in the simpler source rendering.
evaluation.notes: The trigonal-bipyramidal molecule and sp3d orbital views are conceptually correct and well interactive, but the default highlight color and slightly different orientation reduce visual fidelity to the source.
action_items: Remove the default yellow selection highlight, or start in an unselected neutral state matching the source colors.
Adjust the initial camera/orientation of the molecular model so the equatorial chlorines project like the source: one to the right and two to the left.
Consider offering a side-by-side comparison mode so panels (a) and (b) can be viewed simultaneously like the textbook figure.
Reduce or soften the added specular highlight spheres on chlorine atoms to better match the source's simpler ball-and-stick style.
